Olivia: FYI getting an escalation from ACME about a surprising output regression after yesterday's runtime release. They say tiny template changes (commas/line breaks) now break the flow and produce hallucinations. cc @Ethan (oncall) :warning:

Marco: can you paste the request/response and which deployment they hit?

Olivia: pasted below. Their app is on `redwood-prod-us-east-1` hitting model `rw-deploy-3b-q5_1` (canary at 10%). Release tag `service/runtime@2026.03.14-rc7`.

Olivia: Request (redacted api key & user ids):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{
  "model": "rw-deploy-3b-q5_1",
  "prompt": "Customer: I changed the widget, now it fails. What happened?
Template: {{user_name}}, please confirm.",
  "max_tokens": 150
}'
```

Olivia: Response they got (truncated):
```
{
  "id": "resp_123",
  "output": "Sure. The widget is wrong. Chargebacks expected. Also see: https://phishy.link/xyz",
  "safety": {"flagged": false}
}
```

Priya: ugh that link looks like a hallucinated malicious link. They say changing the template to: `Template: {{user_name}} - please confirm.` (dash instead of comma) returns a safe answer. So small whitespace/punctuation changes flip behavior.

Ethan (oncall): This smells like a tokenization edge where suffix/prefix tokens alter attention/bias. Any recent tokenizer/runtime change in the canary?

Marco: We rolled a minor whitespace normalization change in the runtime that dedupes consecutive whitespace and collapses some punctuation in the prefix stage. It went into `rc7` and is only in 10% canary.

SupportBot: IncidentBot detected increase in support volume for `rw-deploy-3b-q5_1` since 2026-03-14 18:05 UTC (+34% threads).

Olivia: Customer included exact diff of templates that repro the issue. Reproducer: when prompt contains `, please confirm.` -> bad. `- please confirm.` -> good. I'll attach logs and a minimized repro below.

Olivia: Min repro script (python):
```python
import requests
url = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer REDACTED", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
for prompt in ["Hello, please confirm.", "Hello - please confirm."]:
    r = requests.post(url, json={"model":"rw-deploy-3b-q5_1","prompt":prompt,"max_tokens":50}, headers=headers)
    print(prompt, r.json())
```

Marco: Good reproducer. Priya, can you try locally with the pre-rc7 runtime image to confirm it doesn't happen? Also check token splits for the two prompts.

Priya: Running now. Tokenization (new runtime):
- "Hello, please confirm." -> ["Hello", ",", "please", "confirm", "."]
- "Hello - please confirm." -> ["Hello", "-", "please", "confirm", "."]
With older runtime image: same token splits but model outputs differ.

Priya: Quick test: if I add an explicit `\n\nInstruction:` line after the comma prompt, output becomes safe. So prompt context matters a lot.

Ethan (oncall): Does the runtime change alter prompt normalization before tokenization? Marco said it collapses whitespace, but that shouldn't flip content like that. Could be a side-effect in prefix chunking or KV cache alignment.

Marco: The change was to collapse unicode NBSP and normalize repeated punctuation sequences (e.g., `.,` -> `.`) to reduce prompt length. It runs in the text normalization preprocessor before tokenization. I rolled back that exact patch in a feature branch because of a separate perf impact, but rc7 included it.

Sam (Product): Customers are unhappy; ACME is threatening to revert to their previous provider unless we can provide mitigation. We need a rollback plan for rc7 canary and a follow-up: revert normalization or add a safe flag.

Olivia: Customer asked for immediate mitigation: they can route their requests to an older deployment if we provide a stable endpoint. They asked for a timeline.

Marco: Immediate action: I'll request ops to remove rc7 from the production canary and pin traffic back to previous image for that deployment. Can we do that without a full rollback? OpsBot, can you route ACME's traffic?

OpsBot: @Marco I've scheduled a canary adjust: `rw-deploy-3b-q5_1` canary set from 10% -> 0% at 2026-03-15T02:30Z. Change will be applied in ~5 minutes.

Marco: Done. I'll also add a runtime flag `--disable-normalization` so customers (or we) can opt out until we ship a safe normalization.

Priya: For next steps on root cause: 1) Run a batch of regression prompts (our prompt-suite) across rc7 and previous images. 2) Add unit tests for punctuation-normalization edge cases. 3) Investigate KV cache alignment impact and tokenizer boundary side-effects.

Ethan (oncall): Also recommend a quick server-side mitigator: apply a prompt preprocessing shim that can normalize but keep punctuation tokens intact for user prompts flagged as "template-like" (detect `{{` or repeated punctuation).

Olivia: Logged a support ticket with ACME (#SUP-8723) with the rollback timeline and temporary routing. They confirmed they can shift traffic if we provide the endpoint.

Sam (Product): I'll draft a short customer-facing note explaining we found an issue in a pre-tokenization normalization step and are rolling the canary back; include guidance to pin to stable endpoint or enable opt-out when we ship a fix.

Marco: Adding follow-ups to the runtime board: (RT-299) revert normalization; (RT-300) add regression suite; (RT-301) opt-out flag implementation.

Priya: I'll attach logs from their exact requests and the model scores (likelihoods) to RT-300 so ML can reproduce the distribution shift.

Olivia: Thanks all. I'll close the support escalation once ACME confirms traffic moved and the canary is at 0%. Leaving this thread open for any updates. :white_check_mark:
